fact_en:
Does a single fixed pulley make lifting heavy things easier?

A single fixed pulley attached to a ceiling does not reduce lifting effort! It only changes the direction of your pull.
fact_bis:
Ginapapasayon ba sa single fixed pulley ang pag-alsa?

Ang usa ka fixed pulley nga gibit sa kisame dili makapamenos sa kusog nga imong pagahikap! Usahay lang niya usbon ang direksyon sa imong pag-uyog.

findings.note: The payload fact is reversed into a hedge: EN "It ONLY changes the direction of your pull" becomes "Usahay lang niya usbon ang direksyon" = "it only SOMETIMES changes the direction". A fixed pulley always redirects the pull — that is its entire function — so the Cebuano-only child learns something false and cannot answer what a fixed pulley does. Compounded by "kusog nga imong pagahikap" (hikap = to TOUCH) for "lifting effort" and "pag-uyog" (uyog = to SHAKE) for "your pull"; nothing in the card restores either.

fact_en:
Why is walking on wet fallen mango leaves so slippery?

The smooth leaf surface reduces friction between your shoes and the ground!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga maluspad ang paglakaw sa basa nga nahulog nga dahon sa mangga?

Hapsay kaayo ang ibabaw sa dahon mao nga maminus ang friction tali sa sapatos ug yuta!

findings.note: The question asks "Ngano nga MALUSPAD ang paglakaw sa basa nga nahulog nga dahon sa mangga?" — luspad = PALE / faded, not slippery (madanglog/madulas). Slipperiness is the effect the whole card explains and it appears nowhere else in the card, so a Cebuano-only child is asked why walking on wet mango leaves is "pale" and never learns that low friction makes you slip. Sibling card ffct-27392 uses "madulas" correctly, which is what this card needed.

fact_en:
Why does a magnet attract an iron nail but not an aluminum soda can?

Aluminum is not a ferromagnetic metal, so the magnet won't attract it!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga gidadani sa magnet ang pako nga puthaw pero dili ang lata nga aluminum?

Ang aluminum dili ferromagnetic, mao nga dili kini dad-on sa magnet!

findings.note: "ang pako nga puthaw" for "an iron nail". In Cebuano pako = WING (or the edible fern); nail is lansang. This is the Tagalog false friend (Tagalog pako = nail). The card never says lansang anywhere, so the Cebuano-only reader is told a magnet attracts an "iron wing" and not an aluminum can — the object the whole demonstration rests on is a different thing.

fact_en:
Can a lemon power a clock?

Yes! A single lemon generates enough electricity through a chemical reaction with metal nails to power a small clock!
fact_bis:
Makapagana ba ang lemon sa orasan?

Oo! Usa ka lemon ra makaproduce og igo nga kuryente pinaagi sa chemical reaction sa metal nga pako aron mapagana ang gamay nga orasan!

findings.note: Same swap: "chemical reaction sa metal nga pako" for "chemical reaction with metal nails" in the lemon-battery card. pako = wing in Cebuano (lansang = nail); nothing in the card restores it, so the child cannot reproduce or picture the setup that makes the lemon generate electricity.

fact_en: Always pull the plastic plug, not the cord, when unplugging appliances! This prevents internal wires from breaking and causing shocks.
fact_bis: Kanunay nga paggukod ang plastic plug, dili ang cord, kung mag-unplug! Makalikay kini sa pagputol sa internal nga mga wire ug malikayan ang shock.

findings.note: Safety card whose verb is wrong in both title and body. Body: "Kanunay nga PAGGUKOD ang plastic plug" — gukod = to CHASE / run after, not to pull (bira). Title: "BATI-A ang Plug Dili Kable" — bati = to feel/hear, not pull. The card is an instruction, and the instruction "pull the plug, not the cord" is never actually stated in Cebuano, so the child cannot perform the action the card exists to teach.

fact_en: Gravity keeps the International Space Station orbiting Earth! Astronauts float in microgravity — not absolute zero gravity. Earth's gravity still pulls them!
fact_bis: Gipabilin sa gravity ang International Space Station sa orbit sa Earth! Naglutaw ang mga astronaut sa microgravity — dili absolute zero gravity. Naay gravity gihapon!

findings.note: title_bis "Grabidad sa Lawak" for "Gravity in Space". In Cebuano lawak = a ROOM / chamber; outer space is kalawakan or kawanangan (Tagalog lawak = expanse — the false-friend route). Corpus evidence that this title is the outlier: ffct-27367 titles the same concept "Kahayag sa Kalawakan" and ffct-27399 asks "Mawala ba ang gravity sa KALAWAKAN?". The title as written reads "Gravity in the Room".

fact_en: Ice has a friction coefficient of just 0.03, making it much slipperier than dry rubber on concrete, which has a friction coefficient of 0.8!
fact_bis: Ang yelo adunay friction coefficient nga 0.03 ra, mao nga mas luspad kini kaysa sa dry rubber on concrete nga adunay friction coefficient nga 0.8!

findings.note: "mas luspad kini kaysa sa dry rubber" — luspad means PALE/faded (colour), not slippery (madanglog/madulas). The card's only conclusion becomes "ice is paler than dry rubber", so a child reads friction 0.03 vs 0.8 as a statement about colour. Nothing else in the card (title "Yelo Friction 0.03") restores slipperiness; sibling card ffct-27485 states the same fact with "kadulas".

fact_en:
Why does a wheelbarrow make heavy garden soil feel so light?

A wheelbarrow is a type of lever! It lets you lift heavy soil with less effort, saving your arm muscles from strain.
fact_bis:
Nganong sayon ma-alsa ang bug-at nga yuta kung mogamit kag ug bangko?

Ang bangko usa ka klase sa lever! Mas sayon nimo ma-alsa ang bug-at nga yuta sa garden nga dili kapoy ang imong bukton.

findings.note: Body calls the wheelbarrow "bangko" (bench/stool) twice, including the core claim "Ang bangko usa ka klase sa lever" — a child learns a BENCH is a lever that lifts soil. Cebuano for wheelbarrow is kariton, which this corpus uses correctly in ffct-27562 and ffct-27589, and even in this card's own title_bis ("Kariton Lever Yuta"), so the body is the outlier and the sentence it breaks is the card's whole fact.

fact_en:
Why does a straw look broken in a glass of water?

Light bends when it enters water because it slows down! This makes a partially submerged straw look broken.
fact_bis:
Nganong murag naputol ang straw sa sulod sa baso nga may tubig?

Mokurot ang suga pag-sulod sa tubig kay hinay-hinay kini! Mao nga murag naputol ang straw nga medyo nasulod.

findings.note: "Mokurot ang suga pag-sulod sa tubig" — kurot means to PINCH, not to bend (liko/bawog). This is the card's explanation for the broken-looking straw and it is the highlighted emph_bis phrase, so the refraction mechanism a child is meant to take away is replaced by "light pinches"; nothing else in the card states that light bends.

fact_en:
Why can an astronaut jump six times higher on the Moon?

The Moon's gravity is only one-sixth of Earth's! This lets an astronaut jump six times higher than on Earth.
fact_bis:
Nganong makatalikod ug unom ka beses nga mas taas ang astronaut sa Buwan?

Ang grabidad sa Buwan usa ka-unom ra sa Yuta! Tungod niini, makatalikod ang astronaut ug unom ka beses nga mas taas.

findings.note: Both the question and the answer use "makatalikod" (to turn one's back) for "jump": "Nganong makatalikod ug unom ka beses nga mas taas ang astronaut sa Buwan?" The card's whole point — you can JUMP six times higher under 1/6 gravity — is replaced by an unrelated action and never restored (lukso never appears); ffct-27582 uses "naglukso-lukso" correctly for the same Moon-gravity fact.

fact_en:
Why is the white sand at Boracay Beach cooler to walk on than dark sand?

The white sand reflects most of the sun's light and heat energy! This keeps the shoreline much cooler than dark volcanic sand.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga mas bugnaw sa tiil ang puti nga balas sa Boracay kumpara sa itom nga balas?

Nag-reflect ang puti nga balas sa kadaghanan sa kahayag ug kainit sa adlaw! Mao nga mas bugnaw ang baybay kumpara sa itom nga bulkanikong balas.

findings.note: title_bis "Pamalandong" is reflection in the MEDITATION/introspection sense only; optical reflection is never called pamalandong in Cebuano. The card is about white Boracay sand reflecting sunlight, and its own body uses "Nag-reflect" (also the emph_bis term), so the title names a different thing than every other field in the card.

fact_en:
Have you ever heard a whisper from far away?

At the Whispering Gallery in London's St. Paul's Cathedral, sound waves travel clearly along the curved wall!
fact_bis:
Nakadungog ka na ba og hunghog gikan sa layo?

Sa Whispering Gallery sa St. Paul's Cathedral sa London, klaro kaayo nga mo-travel ang sound waves sa curved nga bungbong!

findings.note: title_bis "Tunog nga Bulong" — bulong is Cebuano for MEDICINE/remedy (Tagalog false friend: Tagalog bulong = whisper). The card is "Whispering Sound", so the title reads "Medicine Sound". The card's OWN body uses the correct Cebuano "hunghog" (hunghong = whisper), which confirms the title is the outlier.
